20:  * @ref spec/DSL.md#virtualized-lists-lazyvstack--lazyhstack [implements] — LazySelection
21:  *
22:  * App-owned selection and keyboard-focus policy for a lazy container.
23:  *
24:  * The app supplies the selected item index and the native focus flag (hoisted so
25:  * it survives `ViewThatFits` swaps). The component supplies the roving tab stop,
26:  * tap-to-select, arrow/Home/End/Enter navigation, focused-item pinning, and the
27:  * unfocused-list visible-range clamp. It emits the existing focus/key opcodes;
28:  * no new protocol surface is involved.
29:  *
30:  * `selectedIndex` is an item index, including for grids. Grid geometry is
31:  * supplied by the lazy container, so the same object works for stacks and grids.
32:  */
33: class LazySelection(
34:     val selectedIndex: WritableSignal<Int>,
35:     val focusState: WritableSignal<Boolean>,
36:     val onActivate: (Int) -> Unit = {},
37:     /** Called after a tap selects and focuses [index]; use it for click-to-activate. */
38:     val onTap: ((Int) -> Unit)? = null,
39:     /** Handles keys not consumed by navigation or Enter; return true to consume. */
40:     val onKeyDown: ((Int, KeyEvent) -> Boolean)? = null,
41: ) {
42: 
43:     internal fun decorate(
44:         index: Int,
45:         content: View,
46:         geometry: LazySelectionGeometry,
47:         itemCount: Int,
48:     ): View {
49:         val selected = computed { selectedIndex.get() == index }
50:         val isSelected = selected.get()
51:         val requestFocus = computed { focusState.get() && selectedIndex.get() == index }
52:         val tapAction = onTap
53:         val keyAction = onKeyDown
54: 
55:         var row: View = content
56:             .focusable(isSelected)
57:             .focused(requestFocus)
58:             .onKeyDown { key -> handleKey(index, key, geometry, itemCount, keyAction) }
59:             .onTapGesture {
60:                 selectedIndex.set(index)
61:                 focusState.set(true)
62:                 tapAction?.invoke(index)
63:             }
64:         if (isSelected) {
65:             row = row.onFocusChanged { gained ->
66:                 if (gained) {
67:                     focusState.set(true)
68:                     selectedIndex.set(index)
69:                 } else if (selectedIndex.get() == index) {
70:                     focusState.set(false)
71:                 }
72:             }
73:         }
74:         return row
75:     }

79:         if (itemCount <= 0) return null
80:         val selected = index.coerceIn(0, itemCount - 1)
81:         return if (geometry.kind == LazySelectionKind.GRID) {
82:             selected / geometry.tracks.coerceAtLeast(1)

84:             selected

92:     internal fun clampVisible(
93:         firstUnit: Int,
94:         visibleUnits: Int,
95:         itemCount: Int,
96:         geometry: LazySelectionGeometry,
97:     ) {
98:         if (itemCount <= 0 || visibleUnits <= 0 || focusState.get()) return
99:         val tracks = geometry.tracks.coerceAtLeast(1)
100:         val firstItem = (firstUnit.coerceAtLeast(0) * tracks).coerceAtMost(itemCount - 1)

102:         val selected = selectedIndex.get()

105:         }
106:     }

109:         index: Int,
110:         key: KeyEvent,
111:         geometry: LazySelectionGeometry,
112:         itemCount: Int,
113:         keyAction: ((Int, KeyEvent) -> Boolean)?,
114:     ): Boolean {
115:         val next = nextIndex(index, key.keyCode, itemCount, geometry)
116:         if (next != null) {
117:             if (next != index) selectedIndex.set(next)
118:             focusState.set(true)

content.text:
## Findings

- `List` is already a **composite** by contract: `spec/PRIMITIVES.md:183` retires IDs `0x18–0x1A`, and `spec/PRIMITIVES.md:232` defines `List = ScrollView + LazyVStack` with selection via `LazySelection`.
- The style mechanism to mirror is `ButtonStyle`: an environment-scoped interface resolved nearest-wins (`lib/java/.../ButtonStyle.kt`, `lib/rust/.../lib.rs:311`).
- HTML dark mode already works through design tokens: `prefers-color-scheme: dark`, `--pl-dark-*`, `META::SET_COLOR_SCHEME` / `data-pathland-scheme`, and light+dark Tier-1 defaults (`spec/TOKENS.md`, `lib/rust/crates/pathland-render-html/status.md:248-292`). The List gap is that its chrome has no tokens yet.

## Proposed plan

### 1. Authoring surface — no protocol change

Add `ListStyle` as a new style contract, parallel to `ButtonStyle`:

```kotlin
interface ListStyle : Style {
    fun makeBody(config: Configuration): View = config.content()
    fun makeRow(content: View, config: RowConfiguration): View = content
    val rowExtentOverhead: Float get() = 0f
    fun viewportBackground(): Color? = null

    override fun body(content: View): View =
        EnvironmentView.of(content, Environment.LIST_STYLE, this)

    data class Configuration(val content: View, val itemCount: Int?)
    data class RowConfiguration(val index: Int, val itemCount: Int, val selected: Boolean)
}
```

Add `Environment.LIST_STYLE`, `.listStyle(...)` / Rust `.list_style(...)`, and a `List` composite:

- `List(items, itemExtent/itemExtents, key, selection, content)` — lazy path: `ScrollView { LazyVStack { ForEach } }`.
- `List(content)` — static path: eager `VStack`.
- `List` applies the active style’s `makeRow` before `LazySelection` decoration, adds `style.rowExtentOverhead` to lazy extents, and sets `ROLE=LIST` on the row container and `ROLE=LIST_ITEM` on rows.
- Lazy `List` requires an extent (or fixed row height), matching existing `LazyVStack` rules. Static `List` does not.

Rust gets the same `ListStyle`/`List` structure; selection styling remains Kotlin-only for now, consistent with the existing Rust focus/selection gap (#204).

### 2. Built-in styles

Ship all requested styles:

| Style | Viewport | Scroll content | Rows | Separators | Selection |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| `PlainListStyle` | `list.background` | rows as-is | transparent | full width | `list.row.selected.background` |
| `GroupedListStyle` | `list.background` | `list.group.background` | transparent | inset | `list.row.selected.background` |
| `InsetGroupedListStyle` | `list.background` | inset + rounded `list.group.background` | transparent | inset | `list.row.selected.background` |
| `InsetListStyle` | `list.background` | inset rows | transparent | inset | `list.row.selected.background` |
| `SidebarListStyle` | `list.sidebar.background` | sidebar surface | compact | none | `list.sidebar.selected.background` + `list.sidebar.foreground` |

Built-ins use existing primitives only (`VStack`/`LazyVStack`, `Divider`, `background`, `foregroundStyle`, `padding`, `border`, `clipped`). Row-affecting dimensions (vertical padding, separator thickness) stay literal style config values so lazy `ITEM_EXTENT` math is deterministic; colors are token references so dark mode works.

### 3. Design tokens + HTML dark mode

Add `design/tokens/component/list.tokens.json` with light + dark values for:

`list.background`, `list.row.background`, `list.row.selected.background`, `list.separator`, `list.separator.inset`, `list.group.background`, `list.group.inset`, `list.group.radius`, `list.sidebar.background`, `list.sidebar.selected.background`, `list.sidebar.foreground`.

Add a semantic `color.selection` (light/dark alpha accent) for selected-row backgrounds. Extend:

- `lib/rust/crates/pathland-core/src/tokens.rs` `TIER1_TOKENS`
- `lib/rust/crates/pathland-render-core/src/host.rs` concrete light/dark defaults
- `lib/rust/crates/pathland-render-html/src/token_spec.rs` length rules (`list.group.*`, `list.separator.inset`, etc.)
- `spec/TOKENS.md` component-token catalog

Then regenerate: `npm --prefix design run build`, `npm --prefix design run check`, `scripts/sync-design-css.sh`, `cargo run -p pathland-ts-codegen`. The existing Tier-1 CSS test and concrete-defaults test will enforce coverage automatically.

No changes to `spec/protocol.tsv`, `spec/CONFORMANCE.md`, or `spec/engine-traces` because no opcode/property/emission behavior changes.

### 4. Renderer impact

- **HTML (Rust + Java):** no new component code. The List is rendered as its primitive tree; token refs resolve to `var(--pl-list-…)`, and dark mode follows the existing `prefers-color-scheme` / `data-pathland-scheme` machinery. `ROLE=LIST`/`LIST_ITEM` already map to `<ul>/<li>` and the reset styles them.
- **GTK/Qt:** resolve the new Tier-1 tokens through the shared concrete-default tables; verify row/background chrome renders, with unknown-token fallback documented.
- **TS DOM client:** no list-specific code; token application is generic. Regenerate `tokens-core.ts` for the new length rules.

### 5. Specs, status, and tests

Update:
- `spec/DSL.md` — §4.2 `List`, §5.7 `ListStyle` contract, modifier table entry.
- `spec/PRIMITIVES.md` — composite-views table (explain `ListStyle` authoring, no wire change).
- `spec/TOKENS.md` — `color.selection` + `list.*`.
- `lib/rust/crates/pathland-view/status.md`, `lib/java/pathland-view-core/status.md`, both HTML renderer statuses, `pathland-render-core/status.md`; optionally migrate a demo view to `SidebarListStyle` and update `pathland-demo-views-kotlin/status.md`.

Add tests:
- Kotlin `ListTest`: style environment scoping, structure for all five styles, token refs, lazy `ITEM_EXTENT` = content extent + style overhead, variable extents, selection, `ROLE`/`SELECTED`.
- Rust `List` tests: structure, style scoping, token refs, lazy path.
- Kotlin HTML round-trip: assert `var(--pl-list-…)` appears and a `dark.*` List override is emitted in the dark media query.
- Optional `pathland-html-golden` fixture for a List tree, regenerated with `cargo run -p pathland-html-golden -- --emit`.

Verification:
- `cd lib/rust && cargo test`
- `cd lib/java && mvn -P jvm-only test` (or `mvn install`)
- `npm --prefix design run build && npm --prefix design run check`
- `scripts/sync-design-css.sh`
- `cargo run -p pathland-ts-codegen`

## Notes / trade-offs

- No ADR is required: this extends the existing composite + style contract without touching the wire or renderer architecture. If maintainers want decision traceability, a short ADR can be proposed separately.
- Sections, swipe actions, and keyboard/Rust selection parity are follow-ups.
- Built-in styles can be tuned after visual review; the token names and style hooks are the stable part.
On question remains: Swiftui (and other frameworks) has a native list. Will we be able to render that?

Direct answer: **no — not as a platform-native list control.**

With the chosen DSL-composite design, a Pathland `List` emits `SCROLLVIEW + LAZY_VSTACK + rows`. Renderers will produce:

- **HTML:** a scroll container with `<ul>/<li>` semantics via `ROLE=LIST`/`LIST_ITEM`, styled like a list — semantically native HTML, but still DOM rows.
- **GTK/Qt:** `GtkScrolledWindow + GtkBox` / `ScrollView + ColumnLayout`, **not** `GtkListBox`/`QListView`.
- **SwiftUI:** a `ScrollView` containing a lazy stack, **not** SwiftUI's `List` (which maps to `UITableView`/`UICollectionView` on Apple platforms).

The reason is structural: renderers can only map components that exist on the wire. `List` is deliberately not a protocol component — `spec/PRIMITIVES.md:183` retires its IDs, and `spec/PRIMITIVES.md:232` defines it as a composite. A composite gives consistent cross-platform appearance, virtualization, and styling, but it cannot trigger a host's native list widget.

There are three ways forward:

1. **Keep the composite** — accept native-looking chrome + native semantics, not a native widget. No protocol change. This matches the current spec and the plan I proposed.
2. **Add a protocol `LIST` primitive** — map to `List`/`ListBox`/`ListView`/`<ul>`. This enables true native list chrome and row recycling, but requires new component/property definitions, an ADR superseding the current composite contract, and implementation in every renderer. It is a significantly larger change.
3. **Hybrid "native list hint"** — keep the composite rows but add a protocol marker letting a renderer optionally wrap them in a native list. This creates two representations and is fragile; not recommended.

The important decision is whether native widget behavior (native row recycling, swipe actions, native selection/edit modes) is a hard requirement or whether "native-looking and native-semantic" is enough.

Confirmed: the composite approach is the requirement. Final plan below.

## Decision

`List` stays a **DSL-level composite** (`ScrollView + LazyVStack + rows`). This is an explicit **non-goal**: rendering through `SwiftUI.List`, `GtkListBox`, or `QListView` as a single native widget. We get native-looking chrome, native semantic roles on the web (`<ul>/<li>`), lazy windowing, selection, and free dark mode — but not host-native list recycling, swipe actions, native edit mode, or native list internals. Those would require a future protocol-level `LIST` primitive + ADR; the style/token seams here do not block that.

## Implementation plan

1. **Authoring surface (no wire change)**
   - Add `ListStyle` to `pathland-view-core`, environment-scoped like `ButtonStyle` (`Environment.LIST_STYLE`).
   - Hooks: `makeBody(Configuration)` for container/scroll-content chrome, `makeRow(content, RowConfiguration)` for per-row chrome/selection, `rowExtentOverhead`, and optional viewport background.
   - Add `List(items, itemExtent/itemExtents, key, selection)` (lazy) and `List(content)` (eager static). Lazy List requires extents.
   - Apply `ROLE=LIST` to the row container and `ROLE=LIST_ITEM` + `SELECTED` to rows.
   - Mirror the structure in the Rust DSL; Kotlin-only selection is consistent with the existing Rust focus/selection gap.

2. **Built-in styles**
   - `PlainListStyle`, `GroupedListStyle`, `InsetGroupedListStyle`, `InsetListStyle`, `SidebarListStyle`.
   - Built only from existing primitives (`VStack`/`LazyVStack`, `Divider`, background/foreground/padding/border/clip).
   - Row-affecting dimensions stay literal style config so lazy extents remain deterministic; colors are token refs for dark mode.

3. **Tokens + HTML dark mode**
   - Add `design/tokens/component/list.tokens.json` with light + dark values: `list.background`, row/group/sidebar backgrounds, separator + inset, selected backgrounds, sidebar foreground, group inset/radius.
   - Add semantic `color.selection` for selected-row backgrounds.
   - Extend `TIER1_TOKENS`, `concrete_default_tables`, `token_spec.rs` length rules, and `spec/TOKENS.md`.
   - Regenerate design CSS, sync Rust assets, regenerate TS token conventions.
   - HTML dark mode then works through the existing `prefers-color-scheme` / `data-pathland-scheme` / `--pl-dark-*` machinery; no renderer-specific List code.

4. **Specs and status**
   - `spec/DSL.md`: `List` composite, `ListStyle` contract, `.listStyle`.
   - `spec/PRIMITIVES.md`: update the composite-views row and document that no native list widget is implied.
   - `spec/TOKENS.md`: `color.selection` + `list.*`.
   - Update `pathland-view`, `pathland-view-core`, `pathland-render-core`, and both HTML renderer `status.md` files.
   - No changes to `spec/protocol.tsv`, `CONFORMANCE.md`, or engine traces.

5. **Tests**
   - Kotlin/Rust: style scoping, all five styles, token refs, roles, `SELECTED`, lazy extent math, variable extents, selection.
   - End-to-end HTML: `var(--pl-list-…)` refs plus a `dark.*` List override emitted in the dark media query.
   - Design: `npm --prefix design run build && npm --prefix design run check`.
   - Full verification: `cd lib/rust && cargo test`, `cd lib/java && mvn -P jvm-only test`, `scripts/sync-design-css.sh`, `cargo run -p pathland-ts-codegen`.

No ADR is needed for this path because it preserves the existing composite + style contract. A future native-list primitive would be a separate ADR and protocol change.

1: package dev.pathland.view.dsl
2: 
3: import dev.pathland.view.core.Modified
4: import dev.pathland.view.core.PathlandDsl
5: import dev.pathland.view.core.View
6: import java.util.ArrayDeque
7: 
8: /**
9:  * The receiver for view-builder blocks. It carries no members of its own; its
10:  * purpose is to give nested view builders an annotated receiver so an outer
11:  * DSL receiver (a router or modifier config) cannot be captured implicitly.
12:  *
13:  * The builder is synchronous and single-threaded (the same contract as the
14:  * emitter and the environment), so a thread-local child stack is still the
15:  * equivalent of SwiftUI's result builder.
16:  */
17: @PathlandDsl
18: object PathlandScope
19: 
20: /** The thread-local builder child stack the DSL uses to auto-register children. */
21: internal object ViewScopes {
22:     private val stack = ThreadLocal.withInitial { ArrayDeque<MutableList<View>>() }
23: 
24:     fun push(): MutableList<View> {
25:         val scope = mutableListOf<View>()
26:         stack.get().addLast(scope)
27:         return scope
28:     }
29: 
30:     fun pop() {
31:         stack.get().removeLast()
32:     }
33: 
34:     fun current(): MutableList<View>? = stack.get().peekLast()
35: 
36:     fun register(view: View) {
37:         val scope = current() ?: return
38:         // A DSL leaf/container registers its base view as soon as it is constructed.
39:         // A following modifier chain then registers the wrapper; replace the base in
40:         // place so `.padding(16)` on a child is not silently dropped.
41:         val inner = (view as? Modified)?.inner()
42:         if (inner != null) {
43:             val index = scope.indexOfFirst { it === inner }
44:             if (index >= 0) {
45:                 scope[index] = view
46:                 return
47:             }
48:         }
49:         if (scope.none { it === view }) {
50:             scope.add(view)
51:         }
52:     }
53: 
54:     fun unregister(view: View) {
55:         current()?.removeAll { it === view }
56:     }
57: }
58: 
59: /**
60:  * Add a view built outside the DSL builders (e.g. a non-DSL `View` or a
61:  * pre-constructed component) to the current block.
62:  */
63: fun View.add(): View = registerChild()
64: 
65: /** Prefix form: `+prebuiltView`. */
66: operator fun View.unaryPlus(): View = registerChild()
67: 
68: /**
69:  * Collect the views declared by [content]. A newly declared child auto-registers
70:  * into the innermost active scope, so `VStack { Text("a"); Text("b") }` needs no
71:  * `.children(...)` boilerplate.
72:  */
73: fun collectChildren(content: PathlandScope.() -> Unit): List<View> {
74:     val scope = ViewScopes.push()
75:     return try {
76:         PathlandScope.content()
77:         scope.toList()
78:     } finally {
79:         ViewScopes.pop()
80:     }
81: }
82: 
83: internal fun <T : View> T.registerChild(): T {
84:     ViewScopes.register(this)
85:     return this
86: }
87: 
88: /** Collect a ForEach row into one child view (a single child stays unwrapped). */
89: internal fun rowView(content: PathlandScope.() -> Unit): View {
90:     val children = collectChildren(content)
91:     return when (children.size) {
92:         0 -> groupView(emptyList())
93:         1 -> children[0]
94:         else -> groupView(children)
95:     }
96: }

#### List (composite)

`List` is the SwiftUI-shaped row container. It is **not** a protocol component:
it composes `SCROLLVIEW` + `LAZY_VSTACK` (when a row extent is declared) or
`SCROLLVIEW` + `VSTACK` (static content), sets `ROLE=LIST` on the row container
and `ROLE=LIST_ITEM` on each row, and lets the nearest `ListStyle` decorate the
container and rows ([§5.7](#57-styleable-controls-the-style-contract)).

- **Lazy form:** `List(items, itemExtent = …, selection = …) { item, index -> … }`
  or a `Signal<List<T>>` item source. `itemExtent`/`itemExtents` describe the
  **row content** extent; the active style adds its own chrome
  (`rowExtentOverhead`) so the emitted `ITEM_EXTENT` stays stable.
- **Static form:** `List { … }` uses eager rows and needs no extent.
- **Styles:** `PlainListStyle` (default), `GroupedListStyle`,
  `InsetGroupedListStyle`, `InsetListStyle`, `SidebarListStyle`; application
  styles implement `ListStyle`. Apply with `.listStyle(style)`; nearest wins.
- **Dark mode:** built-in styles reference `list.*` design tokens, so the
  renderer resolves their light/dark values without re-emission.
- **Scope:** flat rows only for now; section headers/footers are app-composed or
  a future extension.

These SwiftUI views are **not** protocol primitives. Applications compose them

# pathland-view-core (JVM engine + DSL) — implementation status

**Last updated:** November 22, 2026

The shared, framework-agnostic JVM engine, runtime and authoring DSL for the
Pathland protocol, written in Kotlin. It owns the `View` SPI and shared
authoring vocabulary, the retained-tree diff emitter,
signals/computed/effects, router, cross-platform state, and the
`dev.pathland.view.dsl` SwiftUI-shaped builders/modifiers. The opcode/wire layer
(`dev.pathland.core.protocol`, `.transport`, `.text`, `.markdown`) lives in the
pure-Java `pathland-core` module, which this module depends on. Server and
renderer modules depend on this module; Java hosts consume the Kotlin-authored
views through JVM interop. JNA ring interop lives in the opt-in
`pathland-native-core` module, so this module (and every server/native-image
build) carries no JNA.

## Implemented

- **Opcode/wire layer**: moved to the `pathland-core` module
  (`dev.pathland.core.protocol`, `.transport`, `.text`, `.markdown`). The DSL
  still re-exports the same behaviour through `Text(...)` and the emitter.
- **Signals** (`dev.pathland.view.core.signal`): `signal`/`state`/`computed`/
  `effect`/`untracked`, synchronous glitch-free flush, equality suppression, error
  caching/retry, circular-dependency detection, and a thread-safe global
  `Scheduler`. `Signals.state` binds to the ambient session `PersistentState`
  during a component render.
- **Topic subscriptions** (`dev.pathland.view.core.subscription`): a strongly
  typed `Topic<T, S>` and the DSL `topic(key, subject, initial)` (also
  `Signals.topic`). Scoped topics name an entity subject; `Topic.global(name)`
  declares an unscoped `Topic<T, GlobalSubject>` with the two-argument
  `topic(key, initial)` form. Both return a normal `Signal<T>` backed by a
  session-local mirror; the server runtime registers it with the app's hub and
  applies published values on the session actor. `SessionContext` (thread-local,
  installed by `PathlandSession` around every actor task) also exposes
  `unsubscribe`, `submit`, `isLive` (SSR vs live), and `onClose` (session
  cleanup). Resolution is lazy when a root view's field initializer runs before
  the context is installed.
- **Data sources** (`dev.pathland.view.data`): `AsyncDataSource` loads a small
  list from a blocking or `CompletionStage` loader; `PagedDataSource` loads
  offset/limit pages with a bounded cache, in-flight dedupe, `total`/`loading`/
  `error` signals, and window-driven `ensureLoaded`. A page result outside the
  latest requested window is cached (bounded) but not published to the current
  render; stale failures leave the visible loading/error state alone (ADR-0017;
  `PagedDataSourceTest` covers stale success/failure, `PagedFastScrollTest`
  covers fast back-and-forth and a range before the count). Both apply results
  on the session actor, refresh with a stale-result guard, and close with the
  session;
  SSR starts in the loading state and does not run async work. `ForEach(source)`
  renders loaded rows and placeholders; the lazy stack/grid call `prefetch` for
  the initial and adaptive windows. The optional
  `pathland-view-data-coroutines` module adds `fromSuspend` for both sources.
  Cursor/`hasMore` pages and topic invalidation are planned (ADR-0016 Phase 3–4).
- **State** (`dev.pathland.view.core.state`): `PersistentState`, untyped
  `StateStore`, in-memory store and provider. Kotlin `Component` state delegates
  bind directly before `body()`; the Java `State` field/binder machinery and
  annotation processor are removed.
- **Router** (`dev.pathland.view.core.router`): `Route`, `RouteTable`, `Router`,
  `Navigation`, `NavigationContainer`, `NavigationIntent`, `Params`, `Chrome`,
  `NavOp`. `NavigationLink` and the navigation helpers live in the Kotlin DSL.

# pathland-view (Rust DSL) — implementation status

**Last updated:** November 12, 2026

The SwiftUI-style **view DSL** (`no_std`) building `pathland_engine::Node`
trees. Protocol contract: `spec/`, authoring surface: `spec/DSL.md`.

## Implemented

- **The three authoring operations** (spec/DSL.md §2): every concrete view
  exposes **values** (`Type::with(|c| …)` static / `view.with(|c| …)` chained),
  **modifiers** (`Type::modifiers((A, B))` / `view.modifiers((A, B))`, single or
  tuple list) and, for content-bearing views, **children**
  (`Type::children(vec![…])` / `view.children(vec![…])`). The three may be used
  at creation or chained, in any order.
- **Rich text**: `Text::attributed(...)` / `Text::markdown(...)` and the free
  `attributed_text` / `markdown_text` constructors; `TextConfig::attributed`,
  `attributed_signal`, and `markdown` set `Node::attributed_text` /
  `attributed_binding` (the shared `pathland-markdown` parser is a dependency).
- **Auto-parse**: `Text::new`/`text(...)` and `text_signal`/`TextConfig::text`
  set `Node::markdown_text`, so the engine parses inline Markdown by default;
  `Text::plain`, `Text::plain_signal`, `plain_text`, `TextConfig::plain_text`,
  and `TextConfig::plain_signal` opt out.
- **Per-view `Config`** (`TextConfig`, `StackConfig`, `GridConfig`,
  `RangeConfig`, …) with fluent setters, consumed by the value builders. Values
  move structural properties (`spacing`/`alignment`/grid counts) into the config
  (no longer modifiers).
- **Views**: `VStack`, `HStack`, `ZStack`, `Grid`, `ScrollView` (axis via
  `ScrollAxis` / `.axis(...)`, emitting `SCROLL_AXIS` when horizontal), `LazyVGrid`,
  `LazyHGrid`, `LazyVStack`, `LazyHStack`, `Text`, `Button`, `Spacer`,
  `Icon` (semantic symbols via `IconName` + `icon(…)`), `Image` (sets
  `IMAGE_SOURCE`), `Color` (dual identity: a layout-greedy View *and* a value
  passed into style modifiers), `Shape` + named `Rectangle`/`Circle`/`Capsule`/
  `Ellipse`, `Divider`, `ProgressView`, `Gauge`, `Toggle`, `Slider`,
  `TextField` (sets `PROMPT`), `TextEditor`, `Stepper`, `DatePicker`, `Picker`,
  `Menu`, `ColorPicker` (+ the `vstack!`/`hstack!` macros and
  `text`/`spacer`/`button`/`icon`/`image` free functions).
- **Modifiers** (decoupled values applied via `modifiers(...)`): `Padding`,
  `FontSize`, `FontWeight`, `Font(Font)`, `FontFamily`, `FontDesign` (the enum

# pathland-render-core — implementation status

**Last updated:** October 27, 2026

The **toolkit-free renderer core shared by every Pathland renderer** (GTK4, Qt,
…): opcode-frame decode into a retained native-element description
(`RenderTree` / `HostNode`) plus the design-token resolution contract
(spec/TOKENS.md). Protocol contract: `spec/`. This crate touches **no toolkit**
(no GTK, no Qt) — it is pure protocol + tokens.

## Implemented

- **Window metadata decode**: `RenderTree` stores `META::SET_WINDOW_METADATA` (`WindowMeta`), shared by the GTK/Qt renderers; empty strings clear fields.

- **`RenderTree` / `HostNode`** (extracted from `pathland-render-gtk`'s
  `host.rs`, which was already GTK-free):
  - `TREE` ops → node tree: `CREATE_NODE`, `DELETE_NODE`, `INSERT_CHILD`,
    `REMOVE_CHILD`, `MOVE_CHILD` (append/insert at `u32::MAX`), parent/child
    bookkeeping.
  - `STYLE` ops → node properties: `SET_PROPERTY` (numeric `properties`,
    `STRING` resolved from the arena into `strings`, `DESIGN_TOKEN` refs kept
    in `token_refs`), `SET_TEXT`, `SET_DESIGN_TOKEN` (global overrides, base +
    `dark.` split), and `SET_ATTRIBUTED_TEXT` (decoded into
    `HostNode::attributed`, with the plain `text` fallback populated).
  - Node accessors: `node(id)`, `root()`, string/f32/u32 property helpers,
    `checked()`.
- **Design tokens (spec/TOKENS.md renderer contract)**:
  - `STYLE::SET_DESIGN_TOKEN` overrides stored (base + `dark.*` by path
    prefix; STRING-valued overrides resolved from the arena).
  - `DESIGN_TOKEN`-typed `SET_PROPERTY` values record the token path and
    **resolve at apply time** against the theme, the active scheme, and the
    parent-fallback chain into concrete `properties`/`strings`
    (`resolve_tokens`, reusing `pathland_core::tokens::resolve_ref`); paths
    are kept for re-resolution on scheme change.
  - Explicit `dark.` references resolve the dark layer in either scheme.
  - Previously materialized token values are removed before each resolution,
    so an unresolvable reference (or a reset override) leaves the property
    unset instead of retaining a stale value. A literal `SET_PROPERTY`
    replaces a previous token reference (and vice versa).
  - **Tier-1 default tables** (light + dark) via `concrete_default_tables` —
    concrete platform-appropriate fallbacks; a renderer may enrich with native
    theme colors via `RenderTree::set_defaults`.
  - Platform scheme (`set_scheme`) and application override
    (`set_scheme_override(Option<Scheme>)`, `META::SET_COLOR_SCHEME`) are
    separate; the effective scheme is the override when set.
  - `reset_theme()` / `META::RESET_THEME` clears base + `dark.*` overrides and
    re-resolves against renderer defaults.
  - `concrete_default_tables` now covers the full `TIER1_TOKENS` catalog in
    both schemes (coverage-tested).
- **`render_tree_from_frame`** — decode a fresh tree from one frame.
- **`describe`** — one-opcode human-readable line (debugging aid).

## Consumed by

- `pathland-render-gtk` (decode + token resolution; the GTK-specific
  `tokens.rs` GTK theme-color enrichment stays in that crate).
- `pathland-render-qt` (planned).
- `pathland-view-native` and `pathland-core-transport` dev-tests (decode a
  frame into a `RenderTree` without pulling in a toolkit).

# @pathland/dom-renderer (lib/typescript) — implementation status **Last updated:** November 25, 2026 The **Pathland DOM renderer** — the web client. A vanilla-TypeScript hydration client (no runtime dependencies) that is the single source of the client, replacing the duplicated `app.js` files in the demos. Protocol contract: `spec/`. ## Implemented - **Decoder hardening (issue #63)**: `parseBatch`/`readString`/`readList`/ `readEntryBytes`/`readAttributed` enforce opcode, string-section, list, run/link/attribute, and text-range caps; `applyBatch` validates the whole batch structurally before mutating the DOM (no half-applied batch, unknown value types rejected). Attributed-text links and image/media sources are URL-scheme allowlisted (`javascript:` and non-media `data:` rejected). The transport rejects inbound messages over 2 MiB and closes after five consecutive malformed batches so the reconnect path requests a clean `META::RESYNC`. **SRI**: `copy-to-libs` writes a `sha384-…` second manifest line; the server emits `integrity` on the script tag. - **Attributed text**: decodes `SET_ATTRIBUTED_TEXT` payloads and applies them to the hydrated text element as styled ``/`` runs (v1 attributes: font size/weight/color/style/design/underline/strikethrough). An explicit `SET_TEXT` clears the rich-text marker; plain `TEXT`/`LABEL` updates never wipe rich spans. Full rebuild on payload change; the optional surgical `Range` fast path is deferred. - **Window metadata**: the DOM client applies `META::SET_WINDOW_METADATA` at runtime — `TITLE` → `document.title`, `DESCRIPTION` → meta description, `LOCALE` → ``; empty clears to the renderer default. `LABEL` also names buttons and slider inputs; the media shell is `aria-hidden`. - **Keyboard focus (ADR-0018)**: `META::SET_FOCUS` focuses/blurs a node by id; `A=0, B=0` clears the currently focused element. A node whose `EVENT_LISTENERS` carries the `FOCUS` bit gets `tabindex="0"` (and a `data-pathland-focusable` marker); removing it clears the tab stop. `FOCUS_CHANGED` is reported for any focused node (editing remains text-input only). `KEY_DOWN`/`KEY_UP` map native keys to the canonical table and suppress the platform default for arrows/Home/End/Paging/Enter/Space while leaving Tab native. +
+`List` is the SwiftUI-shaped row container. It is **not** a protocol component:
+it composes `SCROLLVIEW` + `LAZY_VSTACK` (when a row extent is declared) or

+container and rows ([§5.7](#57-styleable-controls-the-style-contract)).

content.text:
Implemented the composite `List` + `ListStyle` path.

**What landed**
- Kotlin: `ListStyle` contract, `Environment.LIST_STYLE`, `.listStyle(...)`, `.selected(...)`, composite `List`, built-in `PlainListStyle`/`GroupedListStyle`/`InsetGroupedListStyle`/`InsetListStyle`/`SidebarListStyle`.
- Rust: `ListStyle`, `list_style(...)`, `List`, matching built-ins, and a `Selected` modifier.
- Rows emit `ROLE=LIST_ITEM` + `SELECTED`; the row container emits `ROLE=LIST`. HTML therefore renders semantic `<ul>/<li>`.
- Lazy lists add the active style’s `rowExtentOverhead` to the app-declared `itemExtent`/`itemExtents`; static `List { … }` stays eager.
- Dark mode: added `list.*` Tier-1 tokens + semantic `color.selection`, light/dark design values, concrete-renderer defaults, token length rules, regenerated CSS/TS artifacts, and golden HTML fixture.
- Specs updated (`DSL.md`, `PRIMITIVES.md`, `TOKENS.md`) plus all affected `status.md` files.
- Fixed TS codegen drift for `SET_FOCUS` and the canonical key constants.

**Verification**
- `mvn -P jvm-only test` passed.
- `npm test` (TS DOM renderer) passed: 329 tests.
- `cargo test` for core/render-core/render-html/view/ts-codegen passed.
- `npm --prefix design run check` passed.

22: /**
23:  * The music player demo root view — an Apple Music-style player authored purely
24:  * with the Kotlin DSL, composed of the [PlayerMainArea] (library + floating
25:  * player bar) and the wide-layout [NowPlayingSidebar].
26:  *
27:  * The root owns the per-session [MediaPlayerService] and scopes it through the
28:  * environment; child views resolve the service instead of receiving its signals
29:  * through their constructors.
30:  */
31: class MusicPlayerView @JvmOverloads constructor(
32:     private val adUrl: String? = null,
33: ) : Component() {
34: 
35:     companion object {
36:         const val SIDEBAR_WIDTH = 280f
37:         const val BAR_HEIGHT = 76f
38: 
39:         // Gray-600: >= 4.5:1 on white, the sidebar, the selected row, and the player bar.
40:         val SECONDARY_FG: Color = Color.rgb(0x4B, 0x55, 0x63)
41:         val ACTIVE_ROW_BG: Color = Color.rgb(0xE8, 0xEF, 0xFF)
42:         val INACTIVE_ROW_BG: Color = Color.rgb(0xE5, 0xE5, 0xEA)
43:         val ACTIVE_ROW_FG: Color = Color.rgb(0x1A, 0x3A, 0x8C)
44:         val SIDEBAR_BG: Color = Color.rgb(0xF6, 0xF7, 0xFA)
45:         val BAR_BORDER: Color = Color.rgb(0xFF, 0xFF, 0xFF)
46:         val BAR_BG: Color = Color.argb(0xBF, 0xEB, 0xEB, 0xED)
47: 
48:         /** A player with no sponsored slot (Java-compatible factory). */
49:         @JvmStatic
50:         fun make(): MusicPlayerView = MusicPlayerView()
51: 
52:         /** A player with a sponsored slot proxying [adUrl] (Java-compatible factory). */
53:         @JvmStatic
54:         fun make(adUrl: String?): MusicPlayerView = MusicPlayerView(adUrl)
55:     }
56: 
57:     private val service by lazy { MediaPlayerService() }
58: 
59:     override fun body(): View {
60:         val mediaPlayer = service
61: 
62:         // One root fit slot selects the complete layout for the window width:
63:         // narrow (no volume, compact transport), medium (volume), wide (volume +
64:         // now-playing sidebar). Keeping the breakpoint at the root avoids a
65:         // nested fit slot whose wide-only children could survive a candidate swap.
66:         val narrowRow = HStack {
67:             PlayerMainArea(wide = false)
68:         }.frame(width = Commands.Size.FILL, height = Commands.Size.FILL)
69: 
70:         val mediumRow = HStack {
71:             PlayerMainArea(wide = true)
72:         }.frame(width = Commands.Size.FILL, height = Commands.Size.FILL)
73: 
74:         val wideRow = HStack {
75:             PlayerMainArea(wide = true)
76:             NowPlayingSidebar(adUrl).clipped()
77:         }.frame(width = Commands.Size.FILL, height = Commands.Size.FILL)
78: 
79:         return VStack {
80:             ViewThatFits(
81:                 Fit(narrowRow),
82:                 Fit(mediumRow, 700f),
83:                 Fit(wideRow, 1024f),
84:             ).frame(width = Commands.Size.FILL, height = Commands.Size.FILL)
85:                 .accessibilityRole(Roles.MAIN)
86:         }.frame(width = Commands.Size.FILL, height = Commands.Size.FILL)
87:             .environment(MediaPlayerService.KEY, mediaPlayer)
88:             .windowMetadata {
89:                 title(computed { "Pathland · " + mediaPlayer.currentTrack.get().title })
90:                 description(computed {
91:                     mediaPlayer.currentTrack.get().artist + " · " + mediaPlayer.currentTrack.get().album
92:                 })
93:                 locale("en")
94:             }
95:     }
96: }

# pathland-demo-views-kotlin — implementation status

**Last updated:** November 22, 2026

Kotlin-owned demo views over `pathland-view-core`, with no Java-DSL dependency.
It owns the app-driven music player and the small sponsored-proxy ad app.

## Structure

- `music/` — the root `MusicPlayerView` (public, Java-mountable).
- `music/model/` — `Track`, `Lyrics`.
- `music/library/` — `LibraryView`, `TrackRowView`.
- `music/player/` — `PlayerMainArea`, `PlayerBar`, `PlayerControls`,
  `TransportControls`, `TrackInfoView`, `VolumeControls`.
- `music/player/controls/` — `SeekControl`, `PercentSeek`, `VolumeControl`.
- `music/service/` — `MediaPlayerService`: per-session player state, playlist,
  `MediaController`, and the environment key shared by the views.
- `music/lyrics/` — `SubtitlePill`.
- `music/sidebar/` — `NowPlayingSidebar`, `UpNextRowView`.
- `ad/` — `AdView`.

## Shared demo support

- **`DemoTheme`** — the demo's global `SET_DESIGN_TOKEN` theme (base + `dark.*`).
- **`DemoAssets`** — the single embedded copy of the 8 audio tracks, 8 album
  covers, and 8 lyric SRT files under
  `META-INF/resources/_pathland/assets/`, plus temp-dir extraction for hosts.
- **`DemoAssetsTest`** — guards all 32 embedded assets and extraction.
- **Responsive-size cover assets** — full 440×440 JPEGs remain for the 220×220
  sidebar; separate 176×176 JPEG thumbnails are used by the smaller track-row
  and player-bar images. Both sets are embedded and extracted for web and GTK.

## Implemented

- **`MusicPlayerView`** — Apple Music-style root: one root `ViewThatFits`
  selects narrow (no volume, compact play-only transport), medium (volume), or
  wide (volume + `NowPlayingSidebar`), with the floating `PlayerBar`.
- **Persisted player state** — owned by `MediaPlayerService` (`player.position`, `player.playing`,
  `player.track`, `player.volume`, `player.seekRequest`, `player.volumeRequest`)
  and created with `Signals.state` while the framework's session state is active.
- **App-driven media** — `MediaPlayerService` owns and registers the
  `MediaController`, and the emitter projects it as a pinned root node; every fit
  candidate shares the same controller. `MEDIA_*` reports feed position/volume
  and `MEDIA_ENDED` advances the track.
- **Seek/volume decoupling** — `SeekControl` buffers drags and commits on release;
  `PercentSeek` maps seconds to 0..100; `VolumeControl` separates report from
  command (each in its own file under `player/controls/`).
- **Lyrics** — synchronized two-line karaoke pill driven by the parsed SRT cues.
- **Window metadata** — track-derived title/description and `locale("en")`.
- **Sponsored proxy** — optional `adUrl` appends a `ProxyView` in the sidebar.
- **`AdView`** — the small sponsored-proxy origin app: a title, a button, and a
  persisted click counter (`ad.clicks`), fully Kotlin-owned and Java-mountable.
- **Accessibility** — transport labels, slider labels, `MAIN`/`HEADER` roles.
- **Windowed library** — `LibraryView` is a `ScrollView` over a `LazyVStack` +
  paged `ForEach` with a fixed 64 pt row extent; `MediaPlayerService` repeats the
  eight base tracks into a 1000-entry playlist and serves 50-row pages with a
  small simulated latency. Loaded rows render `TrackRowView` (a tappable `HStack`
  highlighted by absolute index); unloaded rows render a skeleton placeholder.
  The live/SSR session uses the `PagedDataSource`; emitter-only unit-test mounts
  keep the in-memory list for determinism. The engine's reactive prefetch keeps
  rows rendered ahead of fast scrolling; the demo has no overscan setting.
  Visible-range reports are coalesced latest-wins and stale pages are cached
  without rendering, so a fast scrollbar drag back and forth reuses the visited
  windows instead of showing blank rows and refetching (ADR-0017).
  **Keyboard library navigation (ADR-0018)** — the library uses the shared
  `LazySelection` component: one roving `FOCUS` tab stop on the service's
  ephemeral `focusedIndex`; ↑/↓/Home/End move it, Enter/tap play, Space toggles
  playback. Selection never requests native focus while the list is unfocused,
  so scrolling/clamping cannot steal focus; tapping a row selects and focuses it
  synchronously before playback. Loaded and skeleton rows share the component's
  wrapper; placeholder rows are keyboard-focusable too. The selected row uses a
  blue background while the list is focused and a neutral gray background while
  it is not; text stays black when unfocused. Every row keeps a stable leading
  speaker icon child and the current track reveals it by opacity, so switching
  tracks cannot accumulate stale icons. List rows use the selected background
  as their keyboard indicator and suppress the generic focus outline. Native player-bar controls
  are explicitly tabbable, so Tab leaves the list and reaches the transport
  controls/seek slider under Safari's default keyboard-nav setting as well as
  Chrome. The volume slider carries an explicit 5% `STEP_VALUE`, so each arrow
  press moves it audibly; the seek slider stays continuous (1% per arrow).

## Verified by

`mvn test -pl pathland-demo-views-kotlin` — `LyricsTest`, `SeekControlTest`,
`MediaPlayerServiceTest` (persisted keys, select/next/previous, the 1000-entry
repeated library), `MusicPlayerViewTest` (tree/render, fit swaps, media state,
seek echo guard, snapshot emission, sponsored proxy, and the bounded lazy
library window), `MusicPlayerFitMediaTest` (the pinned media controller survives SSR
snapshot→live and repeated fit crossings; media routing and play stay bound),
and `AdViewTest` (button click / persisted counter delta).

/**
 * A single track row: a playing indicator gutter, cover thumbnail, title/artist,
 * and duration. The selected row is highlighted; the current track's fixed
 * speaker icon is revealed by opacity. Both states are independent and
 * reactive.
 */
internal class TrackRowView(
    private val track: Track,
    private val index: Int,
) : Component() {

    override fun body(): View {
        val service = mediaPlayerService()
        val isCurrent = computed { service.trackIndex.get() == index }
        val isSelected = computed { service.focusedIndex.get() == index }
        val isListFocused = computed { service.listFocused.get() }
        val bg = computed {
            when {
                !isSelected.get() -> Color.CLEAR
                isListFocused.get() -> MusicPlayerView.ACTIVE_ROW_BG
                else -> MusicPlayerView.INACTIVE_ROW_BG
            }
        }
        val fg = computed {
            if (isSelected.get() && isListFocused.get()) MusicPlayerView.ACTIVE_ROW_FG else Color.BLACK
        }
        val playingIconOpacity = computed { if (isCurrent.get()) 1f else 0f }

        return HStack(alignment = VerticalAlignment.CENTER, spacing = 12f) {
            // Keep this child stable: only its opacity changes, so a previous
            // playing track can never leave a stray icon behind.
            Icon(IconName.VOLUME)
                .fontSize(16f)
                .foregroundStyle(MusicPlayerView.ACTIVE_ROW_FG)
                .frame(width = 18f, height = 18f)
                .opacity(playingIconOpacity)

            Image(track.thumbnail)
                .frame(width = 44f, height = 44f)
                .scaledToFit()

            VStack(alignment = HorizontalAlignment.LEADING, spacing = 2f) {
                Text(track.title)
                    .fontWeight(FontWeight.SEMIBOLD)
                    .multilineTextAlignment(TextAlignment.LEADING)
                    .lineLimit(1)

                Text("${track.artist} · ${track.album}")
                    .fontSize(13f)
                    .multilineTextAlignment(TextAlignment.LEADING)
                    .lineLimit(1)
                    .foregroundStyle(MusicPlayerView.SECONDARY_FG)
            }

            Spacer()

            Text(MediaPlayerService.fmt(track.duration))
                .fontSize(13f)
                .foregroundStyle(MusicPlayerView.SECONDARY_FG)
        }
            .accessibilityRole(Roles.LIST_ITEM)
            .background(bg)
            .foregroundStyle(fg)
            .padding(6f)
            .frame { width(Commands.Size.FILL) }
    }
}

 * and a bottom player bar. Asserts the rendered tree and that interactions drive
 * the persisted player state.

class MusicPlayerViewTest {

    private data class Mounted(
        val result: RenderResult,
        val sink: FrameOpcodeSink,
        val store: StateStore,
    )

    private class MultiFrameSink : FrameOpcodeSink() {
        val frames = mutableListOf<ProtocolFrame>()

        override fun endFrame() {
            super.endFrame()
            frames.add(frame())
        }
    }

    private fun mount(snapshot: Boolean = false): Mounted {
        val store = InMemoryStateStore()
        val state = PersistentState(store, "session-1")
        val sink = FrameOpcodeSink()
        val emitter = Emitter(sink)
        if (snapshot) emitter.snapshotEmission(true)
        val result = emitter.mount(MusicPlayerView.make(), Environment(state))
        return Mounted(result, sink, store)
    }

    private fun mountAd(): Mounted {
        val store = InMemoryStateStore()
        val sink = FrameOpcodeSink()
        val emitter = Emitter(sink)
        emitter.snapshotEmission(true)
        val result = emitter.mount(
            MusicPlayerView.make("http://localhost:8080/ad"),
            Environment(PersistentState(store, "session-1")),
        )
        return Mounted(result, sink, store)
    }

    @Test
    fun libraryRendersTracksAndAlbumArt() {
        val frame = mount().sink.frame()

        assertTrue(anySetText(frame, "Building on Solid Ground"))
        assertTrue(anySetText(frame, "Rendered Free"))
        assertTrue(anySetText(frame, "The Pathland Dream"))
        assertTrue(anySetText(frame, "The Foundation"))
        assertFalse(anySetText(frame, "Now Playing"))
        assertTrue(anySetText(frame, "Library"))
        assertTrue(countCreate(frame, Components.IMAGE) >= 3)
        assertTrue(anySetPropertyString(frame, Properties.IMAGE_SOURCE, COVER))
        assertEquals(1, countCreate(frame, Components.VIEW_THAT_FITS))
        assertEquals(1, countCreate(frame, Components.MEDIA_CONTROLLER))
    }

    @Test
    fun libraryUsesAWindowedList() {
        val frame = mount().sink.frame()

        assertEquals(1, countCreate(frame, Components.LAZY_VSTACK))
        assertTrue(anySetProperty(frame, Properties.ITEM_COUNT, 1000))
        assertTrue(anySetProperty(frame, Properties.ITEM_EXTENT, LIBRARY_ROW_HEIGHT))
        assertTrue(anySetProperty(frame, Properties.FIRST_ITEM_INDEX, 0))
        // Only the initial window (20 + overscan 2) is emitted, not 1000 rows.
        assertTrue(countCreate(frame, Components.IMAGE) in 1..40)
    }

    @Test
    fun fitShowsTheSidebarWhenTheParentIsWideEnough() {
        val mounted = mount()
        val slotId = slotIdByMaxThreshold(mounted.sink.frame(), 1024f)
        assertFalse(anySetText(mounted.sink.frame(), "Now Playing"))

        mounted.result.fitInputs()[slotId]!!.accept(2)
        val wide = mounted.sink.frame()

        assertTrue(anySetText(wide, "Now Playing"))
        assertTrue(anySetText(wide, "Up Next"))
        assertEquals(0, countCreate(wide, Components.MEDIA_CONTROLLER))
        assertEquals(0, countCreate(wide, Components.VIEW_THAT_FITS))
    }

    @Test
    fun playerBarRendersTransportAndSliders() {
        val mounted = mount()
        val frame = mounted.sink.frame()

        // The narrow player bar has the play/pause transport button; the
        // library rows are tappable HStacks, not buttons.
        assertTrue(countCreate(frame, Components.BUTTON) >= 1)
        assertEquals(1, countCreate(frame, Components.SLIDER))
        assertTrue(anySlider(frame, 0f, 100f))
        assertTrue(anySetText(frame, "|"))
        assertTrue(anySetPropertyString(
            frame,
            Properties.MEDIA_SOURCE,
            "/_pathland/assets/audio/track1.mp3",
        ))
        assertTrue(anySetProperty(frame, Properties.PLAYBACK_STATE, 0))
        assertTrue(anySetProperty(frame, Properties.MEDIA_POSITION, 0f))

        val rootSlot = slotIdByMaxThreshold(frame, 1024f)
        mounted.result.fitInputs()[rootSlot]!!.accept(1)
        val medium = mounted.sink.frame()
        assertTrue(anySlider(medium, 0f, 1f))
        assertTrue(anySliderValue(medium, 0.7f))
        assertTrue(anySetProperty(medium, Properties.STEP_VALUE, 0.05f), "volume has a usable 5% keyboard step")

        mounted.result.fitInputs()[rootSlot]!!.accept(2)
        val withSidebar = mounted.sink.frame()
        assertTrue(anySetText(withSidebar, "Now Playing"))
        assertTrue(anySetText(withSidebar, "Up Next"))
    }

    @Test
    fun snapshotEmissionCarriesEveryCandidate() {
        val mounted = mount(snapshot = true)
        val frame = mounted.sink.frame()

        assertTrue(anySetText(frame, "Library"))
        assertTrue(anySetText(frame, "Now Playing"))
        val rootSlot = slotIdByMaxThreshold(frame, 1024f)
        assertEquals(3, childCount(frame, rootSlot))
    }

    @Test
    fun interactionDrivesPersistedPlayerState() {
        val mounted = mount()
        for (tap in mounted.result.tapActions().values.toList()) {
            tap.run()
        }
        val track = mounted.store.load("player.track:session-1", Integer::class.java)
        val playing = mounted.store.load("player.playing:session-1", java.lang.Boolean::class.java)
        assertTrue(track.isPresent || playing.isPresent)
    }

    @Test
    fun mediaEventsDriveThePlayerState() {
        val store = InMemoryStateStore()
        val state = PersistentState(store, "session-1")
        val sink = FrameOpcodeSink()
        val result = Emitter(sink).mount(MusicPlayerView.make(), Environment(state))
        val dispatcher = InputDispatcher(result, Signals.signal("/"))

        val audioId = result.mediaInputs().keys.first()
        dispatcher.dispatch(Event.mediaTimeUpdated(audioId, 12.5f))
        assertEquals(12.5f, store.load("player.position:session-1", java.lang.Float::class.java).get())

        val media = result.mediaInputs().values.first()
        media.onVolumeChanged(0.5f)
        assertEquals(0.5f, store.load("player.volume:session-1", java.lang.Float::class.java).get())
        media.onEnded()
        assertTrue(store.load("player.track:session-1", Integer::class.java).isPresent)
    }

        store.save("player.playing:session-1", true)
        val state = PersistentState(store, "session-1")
        val sink = MultiFrameSink()
        val result = Emitter(sink).mount(MusicPlayerView.make(), Environment(state))
        val before = sink.frames.size

        result.mediaInputs().values.first().onEnded()

        val deltas = sink.frames.subList(before, sink.frames.size)
        assertTrue(deltas.any {
            anySetPropertyString(it, Properties.MEDIA_SOURCE, MediaPlayerService.TRACKS[1].audio)
        })
        assertFalse(deltas.any { anyProperty(it, Properties.PLAYBACK_STATE) })
    }

content.text:
## Plan: left navigation sidebar in the music player demo

### Layout
- Add a new left navigation sidebar (`NavigationSidebar`) at **220pt** wide.
- Responsive candidates become:
  - **Narrow (<960):** current compact layout, no left sidebar.
  - **Medium (960–1023):** `NavigationSidebar + PlayerMainArea(wide = true)`; no Now Playing.
  - **Wide (≥1024):** `NavigationSidebar + PlayerMainArea(wide = true) + NowPlayingSidebar` on the right.
- Raise the medium `Fit` threshold from `700f` to `960f` so the full player bar still fits beside the sidebar.
- Now Playing remains wide-only, as requested.

### New sidebar content
- New file: `music/sidebar/NavigationSidebar.kt`.
- Header `Music`, then a static `List` using the new `SidebarListStyle` with:
  - `Library` — folder icon, selected by default
  - `Playlists` — list icon
  - `Artists` — users icon
  - `Albums` — grid icon
  - `Songs` — music icon
- The list is locally interactive (tap/arrow selection highlights a row) but does **not** navigate or filter yet.
- Use `List` + `SidebarListStyle` so it exercises the new list chrome and inherits light/dark token styling.
- Background/foreground use `list.sidebar.*` tokens; add a light/dark `list.sidebar.background` override in `DemoTheme` to match the existing `SIDEBAR_BG` palette.

### State
- Add `navIndex` and `navFocused` signals to `MediaPlayerService`, hoisted like the library’s `focusedIndex`/`listFocused` so selection survives `ViewThatFits` candidate swaps.
- Default `navIndex = 0` (Library).

### Files
- Add `lib/java/pathland-demo-views-kotlin/src/main/kotlin/dev/pathland/demo/music/sidebar/NavigationSidebar.kt`
- Update `MusicPlayerView.kt` (import, `NAV_SIDEBAR_WIDTH`, medium/wide rows, 960 breakpoint, doc).
- Update `MediaPlayerService.kt` (nav signals).
- Update `DemoTheme.java` (`list.sidebar.background` light/dark).
- Update `pathland-demo-views-kotlin/status.md` (structure + behavior).

### Tests
- Extend `MusicPlayerViewTest`:
  - Narrow has no `Playlists`/`Artists`/`Albums`/`Songs` and no Now Playing.
  - Accepting medium (index 1) shows the navigation labels and still no Now Playing.
  - Accepting wide (index 2) shows both navigation and Now Playing.
  - Snapshot emission includes the navigation sidebar in medium/wide candidates.
- Verify existing fit/media tests still pass (controller pinning, slider counts, fit crossings).
- Add a focused `NavigationSidebarTest` if useful to assert the five rows, default selected Library row, and `SidebarListStyle` token usage.

### Verification
- `mvn -q -pl pathland-demo-views-kotlin -am test`
- `mvn -q -P jvm-only test`
- Optionally run the Quarkus/Spring demo and check the medium/wide layouts visually.

No protocol or spec changes are involved; this is demo-view work plus a demo theme override.

/** One static navigation section in the left sidebar. */
private data class NavigationItem(val label: String, val icon: IconName)

/**
 * The Apple Music-style left navigation sidebar: a compact, static section list
 * (Library/Playlists/Artists/Albums/Songs) using the DSL `List` with
 * `SidebarListStyle`. Selection is local visual feedback only; navigation and
 * filtering are future work.
 */
internal class NavigationSidebar : Component() {

    private val items = listOf(
        NavigationItem("Library", IconName.FOLDER),
        NavigationItem("Playlists", IconName.LIST),
        NavigationItem("Artists", IconName.USERS),
        NavigationItem("Albums", IconName.GRID),
        NavigationItem("Songs", IconName.MUSIC),
    )

    override fun body(): View {
        val service = mediaPlayerService()
        val selection = LazySelection(service.navIndex, service.navFocused)

        return VStack(alignment = HorizontalAlignment.LEADING, spacing = 12f) {
            Text("Music")
                .font(Font.largeTitle())
                .fontSize(22f)
                .fontWeight(FontWeight.BOLD)

            PathlandList(selection = selection) {
                items.forEach { item -> NavigationRow(item) }
            }.listStyle(SidebarListStyle)
        }
            .padding(16f)
            .background(CoreColor.token("list.sidebar.background"))
            .foregroundStyle(CoreColor.token("list.sidebar.foreground"))
            .frame(
                width = MusicPlayerView.NAV_SIDEBAR_WIDTH,
                height = Commands.Size.FILL,
            )
    }

    private fun NavigationRow(item: NavigationItem): View =
        HStack(alignment = VerticalAlignment.CENTER, spacing = 10f) {
            Icon(item.icon)
                .fontSize(16f)
                .frame(width = 18f, height = 18f)
            Text(item.label)
                .fontSize(14f)
                .fontWeight(FontWeight.SEMIBOLD)
            Spacer()
        }
}

content.text:
Added the left navigation sidebar to the music player demo.

- New `NavigationSidebar` with Library, Playlists, Artists, Albums, and Songs, using the new `List` + `SidebarListStyle`.
- Layout now:
  - Narrow `<960`: no sidebar, compact player.
  - Medium `960–1199`: left nav + full player bar.
  - Wide `≥1200`: left nav + full player bar + right Now Playing panel.
- Now Playing is wide-only.
- Nav selection is local visual feedback, with selection/focus state on `MediaPlayerService` so it survives fit-candidate swaps.
- Added demo theme overrides for `list.sidebar.background` in light and dark.
- Updated tests and `status.md`.

Verification: `mvn -q -pl pathland-demo-views-kotlin -am test` passes.
Can we then add some real navigation to the sidebar?

content.text: Today the sidebar only changes a local highlight. “Real navigation” can mean either in-place section switching or URL-routed navigation. The framework supports both, but they have different tradeoffs.

questions.question: What should clicking a sidebar item actually do?

options.label: In-place section switching (Recommended)
options.description: The selected section drives the main pane. No URL change; keeps the existing keyboard/focus selection and is the smallest reliable step.

options.label: Routed URL navigation
options.description: Use the existing Router/NavigationContainer so sections get URLs (/albums, /artists, …), deep links, and browser back/forward. More framework wiring and tests; selection follows the route.

options.label: Router as source of truth + keyboard
options.description: Route-backed sections plus explicit sidebar keyboard navigation. Most complete, but the largest change.

questions.question: How much real content should the sidebar sections get?

options.label: Practical five sections (Recommended)
options.description: Library/Songs show the track list; Albums and Artists show grouped lists from the existing tracks; Playlists shows a small static playlist list. Detail drill-down can follow later.

options.label: Full navigation with drill-down
options.description: Albums → album detail, Artists → artist detail, Playlists → playlist tracks, plus the main section lists. Much larger scope.

options.label: Library/Songs only
options.description: Library and Songs switch the track list; Playlists/Artists/Albums show a simple placeholder for now.

questions.question: Should the selected section survive a page reload/session?

options.label: No, reset to Library (Recommended)
options.description: Keep it ephemeral like the current nav selection; simpler and avoids demo state noise.

options.label: Yes, persist it
options.description: Store the section in PersistentState so a reload restores the last section (unless routed URLs make this unnecessary).

content.text: One detail to settle: routed navigation already stores the section in the URL, so a reload of `/albums` stays on Albums and a deep link works. Do you still want an additional persisted “last section” fallback?

questions.question: How should persistence work now that navigation is URL-routed?

options.label: URL is the persistence (Recommended)
options.description: Reloading/deep-linking /albums restores Albums; a bare / always means Library. No extra persisted state, no redirects.

options.label: Persist last section + redirect /
options.description: Store the last section in PersistentState and redirect a bare / to it. Reopens the last section but an explicit / no longer means Library.

options.label: Persist only without a URL
options.description: Use URL routing on web; keep a persisted fallback only for desktop/native hosts that have no URL.

/**
 * One "Up next" / "Then" track line in the now-playing sidebar.
 *
 * Tapping the row selects that track in the shared player service.
 */
internal class UpNextRowView(private val offset: Int) : Component() {

    override fun body(): View {
        val service = mediaPlayerService()

        return Text(computed {
            val track = service.trackAt(offset)
            (if (offset == 1) "Up next · " else "Then · ") + track.title + " — " + track.artist
        }).fontSize(13f)
            .foregroundStyle(MusicPlayerView.SECONDARY_FG)
    }
}

/** One static navigation section in the left sidebar. */
private data class NavigationItem(val label: String, val icon: IconName)

/**
 * The Apple Music-style left navigation sidebar: a compact, static section list
 * (Library/Playlists/Artists/Albums/Songs) using the DSL `List` with
 * `SidebarListStyle`. Selection is local visual feedback only; navigation and
 * filtering are future work.
 */
internal class NavigationSidebar : Component() {

    private val items = listOf(
        NavigationItem("Library", IconName.FOLDER),
        NavigationItem("Playlists", IconName.LIST),
        NavigationItem("Artists", IconName.USERS),
        NavigationItem("Albums", IconName.GRID),
        NavigationItem("Songs", IconName.MUSIC),
    )

    override fun body(): View {
        val service = mediaPlayerService()
        val selection = LazySelection(service.navIndex, service.navFocused)

        return VStack(alignment = HorizontalAlignment.LEADING, spacing = 12f) {
            Text("Music")
                .font(Font.largeTitle())
                .fontSize(22f)
                .fontWeight(FontWeight.BOLD)

            PathlandList(selection = selection) {
                items.forEach { item -> NavigationRow(item) }
            }.listStyle(SidebarListStyle)
        }
            .padding(16f)
            .background(CoreColor.token("list.sidebar.background"))
            .foregroundStyle(CoreColor.token("list.sidebar.foreground"))
            .accessibilityRole(Roles.NAVIGATION)
            .frame(
                width = MusicPlayerView.NAV_SIDEBAR_WIDTH,
                height = Commands.Size.FILL,
            )
    }

    private fun NavigationRow(item: NavigationItem): View =
        HStack(alignment = VerticalAlignment.CENTER, spacing = 10f) {
            Icon(item.icon)
                .fontSize(16f)
                .frame(width = 18f, height = 18f)
            Text(item.label)
                .fontSize(14f)
                .fontWeight(FontWeight.SEMIBOLD)
            Spacer()
        }
}

content.text:
## Plan: real sidebar navigation in the music player demo

### Navigation model
Use the existing **Router + NavigationContainer**, bound to the host’s `Platform.ACTIVE_PATH` signal.

Route map:

| Sidebar item | Path | Content |
|---|---|---|
| Library | `/` | existing full track list |
| Playlists | `/playlists` | static playlist list |
| Artists | `/artists` | unique artists from the demo tracks |
| Albums | `/albums` | unique albums from the demo tracks |
| Songs | `/songs` | full track list titled “Songs” |

- Sibling sections use `router.navigate(path)` (no back-stack push).
- Browser back/forward and deep links work through the existing `ROUTE` → `pushState` path.
- Unknown paths fall back to Library.
- **Persistence is the URL**: reloading `/albums` restores Albums; no new `PersistentState` key.

### Wiring
- `MusicPlayerView` creates one router lazily on first render, bound to `Environment.value(Platform.ACTIVE_PATH)`, created inside `Signals.untracked` so route reads do not subscribe the whole root.
- Route destinations are fixed view instances (stable identity), created once in the route table:
  - `LibraryView("Library")`
  - `LibraryView("Songs")` (parameterize the existing header)
  - `PlaylistsView()`
  - `ArtistsView()`
  - `AlbumsView()`
- `PlayerMainArea` places `NavigationStack(router)` in the content slot, under the floating player bar, so the bar and now-playing panel persist across section changes.
- `NavigationSidebar(router)` uses a `RouteIndexSignal` adapter (`WritableSignal<Int>`): `get()` maps `router.routeSignal().get().pathOnly()` to the section index; `set()` calls `router.navigate(path)`.
  - `LazySelection` receives this adapter, so tap and arrow-key navigation both update the route.
  - Selected highlight follows the route, including browser back/forward and deep links.
- Remove the ephemeral `navIndex` from `MediaPlayerService`; keep `navFocused` for ephemeral keyboard focus.

### Section content (practical five sections, no drill-down)
- `LibraryView` gains a `title` parameter; `/` and `/songs` reuse it.
- `AlbumsView`: header + unique-album rows (cover, album, artist, song count), `ROLE=LIST`/`LIST_ITEM`.
- `ArtistsView`: header + unique-artist rows (cover, artist, album count), same roles.
- `PlaylistsView`: header + a small static playlist list (“All Songs”, “Pathland Essentials”, “Recently Added”, “Flow”), with cover and song count.
- Add `albums` and `artists` derived lists to `MediaPlayerService` from the base tracks.
- No album/artist/playlist detail routes yet; rows are display-only.

### Files
- Update `MusicPlayerView.kt` (router creation, route table, pass router to nav/main).
- Update `NavigationSidebar.kt` (router param, section paths, `RouteIndexSignal`, remove local-only wording).
- Update `MediaPlayerService.kt` (remove `navIndex`, add `albums`/`artists`).
- Update `PlayerMainArea.kt` (render `NavigationStack(router)`).
- Update `LibraryView.kt` (title parameter).
- Add `AlbumsView.kt`, `ArtistsView.kt`, `PlaylistsView.kt` under `music/library/`.
- Update `pathland-demo-views-kotlin/status.md`.

### Tests
- Add router/deep-link tests:
  - Mount with active path `/albums` → Albums content.
  - Mount with active path `/artists`, `/songs`, `/playlists` → correct content.
  - Unknown path `/nope` → Library fallback.
  - Update the active path signal after mount → content swaps.
  - Click/tap the sidebar “Playlists” row → route changes and content becomes Playlists.
- Keep existing fit/media tests; update only if the extra navigation slot changes expected tree counts.
- Verify medium/wide layouts still show the nav sidebar and Now Playing remains wide-only.

### Verification
- `mvn -q -pl pathland-demo-views-kotlin -am test`
- `mvn -q -P jvm-only test`
- Optional: run the Quarkus/Spring demo and check deep links (`/albums`, `/artists`) plus browser back/forward.

No protocol, renderer, or spec changes are involved; this is demo-view wiring on top of the existing router.

content.text:
## Plan: sidebar label styling + Tailwind-aligned sidebar tokens

### 1. Make `SidebarListStyle` define the row label style

Analogous to SwiftUI `.listStyle(.sidebar)` styling the inner `Label`:

- Add a private `SidebarLabelStyle(selected: Signal<Boolean>) : LabelStyle`.
- `SidebarListStyle.makeRow(...)` applies it to the row content:
  ```kotlin
  content.labelStyle(SidebarLabelStyle(config.selected()))
  ```
- Update the demo sidebar rows to use a real `Label`:
  ```kotlin
  Label(item.label) { Icon(item.icon) }
  ```
- `SidebarLabelStyle` renders:
  - `HStack` with `gap-x-3` spacing
  - `size-6` icon
  - `text-sm` semibold title
  - default/selected icon and text colors
- Any explicit `.labelStyle(...)` closer to the `Label` still wins (environment nearest-wins).
- Document this in `spec/DSL.md` §5.7: a list style may scope a label style over its rows.

### 2. New/updated design tokens

Yes — a small set of `list.sidebar.*` tokens makes sense. They are component-scoped, carry light/dark values, and keep the global semantic palette clean.

| Token | Light | Dark | Tailwind mapping |
|---|---|---|---|
| `list.sidebar.background` | `{color.surface}` | `{color.surface}` | `bg-white` / `dark:bg-gray-900` (already matches) |
| `list.sidebar.foreground` **(update)** | `{base.color.gray.700}` | `{base.color.gray.400}` | default `text-gray-700` / `dark:text-gray-400` |
| `list.sidebar.selected.background` **(update)** | `{base.color.gray.50}` | `{base.color.white-a05}` | `bg-gray-50` / `dark:bg-white/5` |
| `list.sidebar.selected.foreground` **(new)** | `{base.color.indigo.600}` | `{base.color.white}` | selected text |
| `list.sidebar.icon.foreground` **(new)** | `{base.color.gray.400}` | `{base.color.gray.400}` | default icon |
| `list.sidebar.selected.icon.foreground` **(new)** | `{base.color.indigo.600}` | `{base.color.white}` | selected icon |
| `list.sidebar.row.radius` **(new)** | `{base.radius.sm}` | `{base.radius.sm}` | `rounded-md` (6px) |
| `list.sidebar.label.gap` **(new)** | `{base.space.3}` | `{base.space.3}` | `gap-x-3` (12px) |
| `list.sidebar.icon.size` **(new)** | `{base.space.6}` | `{base.space.6}` | `size-6` (24px) |
| `list.sidebar.label.font.size` **(new)** | `{base.font.size.14}` | `{base.font.size.14}` | `text-sm` (14px) |

- `font-semibold` uses the existing `FontWeight.SEMIBOLD` (600); no new token needed.
- Component tokens that reference the base palette get `$extensions.pathland.baseReference` justifications (required by the design checker).
- Add new tokens to `TIER1_TOKENS`, `concrete_default_tables`, `token_spec.rs` length rules, `spec/TOKENS.md`, and `design/tokens/component/list.tokens.json`.
- Regenerate `design/build`, sync the Rust HTML assets, regenerate TS token conventions, and regenerate the HTML golden document fixture.

### 3. `SidebarListStyle` visual changes

- Row padding becomes uniform **8px (`p-2`)**; no separators.
- `rowExtentOverhead` becomes `16f`.
- Apply `list.sidebar.row.radius` to the row.
- Apply selected/default foreground at row level for non-`Label` content too.
- Apply sidebar label style for `Label` content.
- Keep the existing `list.sidebar.background` viewport/container.

### 4. What we intentionally do not tokenize

- **Row padding / row height**: these affect lazy `ITEM_EXTENT` math; they stay literal style geometry so virtualization stays deterministic.
- **Hover / pressed / focus styles**: the protocol explicitly leaves interaction states to renderers. The Tailwind `hover:bg-gray-50` / `hover:text-indigo-600` look cannot be encoded in `ListStyle` without a renderer-owned hook. We can add that later as a deliberate HTML-renderer sidebar CSS feature; it would not be a protocol/list-style property.
- **Dark ring** (`dark:ring-white/10`): optional follow-up; would be a demo/renderer container treatment, not list row style.

### 5. Rust parity

- Update `SidebarListStyle` row padding to 8/8 and apply `list.sidebar.row.radius`.
- Rust has no `Label` view, so the label-style hook is Kotlin/JVM-only for now. The updated color tokens still retheme Rust sidebar rows.

### 6. Files and verification

Update:
- `lib/java/pathland-view-core/.../dsl/List.kt`
- `lib/java/pathland-view-core/.../dsl/Styles.kt` (or keep the label style private in `List.kt`)
- `lib/java/pathland-demo-views-kotlin/.../sidebar/NavigationSidebar.kt`
- `design/tokens/component/list.tokens.json`
- `lib/rust/crates/pathland-core/src/tokens.rs`
- `lib/rust/crates/pathland-render-core/src/host.rs`
- `lib/rust/crates/pathland-render-html/src/token_spec.rs`
- `lib/rust/crates/pathland-view/src/lib.rs` (Rust sidebar padding/radius)
- `spec/DSL.md`, `spec/TOKENS.md`
- affected `status.md` files
- regenerated CSS/TS/golden HTML assets

Verify:
- `npm --prefix design run build && npm --prefix design run check`
- `scripts/sync-design-css.sh`
- `cargo run -p pathland-ts-codegen`
- `cargo run -p pathland-html-golden -- --emit`
- `cargo test -p pathland-view -p pathland-render-core -p pathland-render-html`
- `mvn -q -pl pathland-view-core -am test`
- `mvn -q -pl pathland-demo-views-kotlin -am test`
- `mvn -q -P jvm-only test`

The main open question is hover: I recommend leaving it renderer-owned for now and aligning the static/default/selected design exactly. If you want the Tailwind hover treatment immediately, I can add a renderer-owned sidebar CSS hook as a separate step.
Can you suggest meaningful semantic tokens or reuse existing ones? If possible no renderer owned CSS, as this is a composite.
