spec/TOKENS.md:112:| `color.accent` | Accent for controls (focus, selection, toggle fill) |
## Standard Token Catalog

The catalog is layered. **Tier 1 (core)** tokens are mandatory: a renderer MUST
provide light and dark defaults and resolve them. **Tier 2 (extended)** tokens
are recommended: a renderer SHOULD provide defaults, and an application MAY
override them; a renderer that cannot apply a Tier 2 token ignores it (the same
"allowed and ignored" rule as unapplicable modifiers).

Default values are **renderer-owned and platform-appropriate**; the tables below
name the tokens and their *meaning*, never concrete values. The renderer MUST
resolve tokens by name and MAY map them onto native semantic resources (e.g. the
platform's system text color for `color.text.primary`).

### Colors — Tier 1

| Token | Meaning |
|-------|---------|
| `color.primary` | Primary brand / accent fill |
| `color.secondary` | Secondary brand / accent fill |
| `color.background` | Document / canvas background |
| `color.surface` | Raised surface (cards, panels, popovers) |
| `color.text.primary` | Primary text color |
| `color.text.secondary` | Secondary / muted text color |
| `color.text.onPrimary` | Text placed on a `color.primary` fill |
| `color.border` | Default border / outline color |
| `color.accent` | Accent for controls (focus, selection, toggle fill) |

Tier 2: `color.separator` (hairline dividers), `color.selection` (selected-row
/ selection highlight), and status colors `color.success`, `color.warning`,
`color.danger`, `color.info`.

### Typography — Tier 1 core

| Token | Meaning |
| `opacity.disabled` | The renderer MAY apply this to disabled controls. The disabled **state** itself is the `ENABLED` property; its visual handling (including this opacity) remains renderer-owned. |

### Shared control core — Tier 1

Tokens every control-style component (buttons, inputs, switches, sliders, …)
shares. Renderers MUST resolve these; an individual token a renderer cannot
apply is ignored.

| Token | Meaning |
|-------|---------|
| `control.background` | Control resting background |
| `control.foreground` | Control content (label/icon) color |
| `control.border` | Control border color |
| `control.border.width` | Control border width |
| `control.radius` | Control corner radius |
| `control.padding.horizontal` / `control.padding.vertical` | Control inner padding |
| `control.height` | Control height (F32) |
| `control.font.size` / `control.font.weight` | Control text |
| `control.accent` | Control accent (fill, selection, focus) |

### Per-component tokens

Small sets; only where a component's semantics genuinely differ from
`control.*`. All Tier 1 unless noted.

**Buttons** (Tier 1): `button.background`, `button.foreground`, `button.border`,
`button.radius`, `button.padding`, `button.height`, `button.font.size`,
`button.font.weight`, `button.accent`.

> A composite shorthand such as `button.padding` (two-axis) is renderer-owned:
> the scalar token value types cannot encode a multi-part CSS shorthand. Apps
> that need a scalar override should use the shared control padding tokens or
> per-component properties.

**Text fields / editors** (Tier 1): `input.background`, `input.foreground`,
`input.placeholder`, `input.border`, `input.radius`, `input.font.size`.

**Toggle / switch** (Tier 1): `toggle.accent`, `toggle.track.off`,
`toggle.track.on`, `toggle.thumb`.

**Slider** (Tier 1): `slider.accent`, `slider.track`, `slider.thumb`.

**Progress / gauge** (Tier 1): `progress.track`, `progress.fill`,
`gauge.track`, `gauge.fill`.

**Stepper** (Tier 2): `stepper.accent`, `stepper.background`, `stepper.border`,
`stepper.radius`.

**Picker** (Tier 2): `picker.accent`, `picker.background`, `picker.border`,
`picker.radius`.

**Menu** (Tier 2): `menu.background`, `menu.foreground`, `menu.border`,
`menu.radius`.

**Label** (Tier 2): `label.foreground`, `label.font.size`.

content.text:
Yes. I would avoid adding a large `list.sidebar.*` visual vocabulary and instead add a small semantic layer, then reuse the existing scale/control tokens. This keeps the sidebar composite fully token-driven with no renderer-owned CSS.

## Recommended semantic additions (4)

Add these to `spec/TOKENS.md` as Tier 2 semantic colors:

| Semantic token | Light | Dark | Why |
|---|---|---|---|
| `color.text.body` | `{base.color.gray.700}` | `{base.color.gray.400}` | Default navigation text (`text-gray-700` / `dark:text-gray-400`) |
| `color.icon.muted` | `{base.color.gray.400}` | `{base.color.gray.400}` | Default sidebar icons |
| `color.selection.subtle` | `{base.color.gray.50}` | `{base.color.white-a05}` | Neutral selected-row background (`bg-gray-50` / `dark:bg-white/5`) |
| `color.text.onSelection` | `{base.color.indigo.600}` | `{base.color.white}` | Selected text/icon (`text-indigo-600` / `dark:text-white`) |

`color.selection` stays as the accent selection highlight for other list styles; the sidebar uses the neutral `color.selection.subtle`.

## Reuse existing tokens

| Tailwind | Reuse |
|---|---|
| `bg-white` / `dark:bg-gray-900` | `color.surface` |
| `rounded-md` (6px) | `control.radius` |
| `text-sm` (14px) | `control.font.size` |
| `font-semibold` (600) | `FontWeight.SEMIBOLD` / `control.font.weight` |
| `gap-x-3` (12px) | `space.3` |
| `size-6` (24px) | `space.6` |
| `p-2` (8px) | Row padding **8px literal** (see note below) |
| `space-y-1` (4px) | A 2px top/bottom transparent inset outside the row background, so adjacent rows have a 4px gap |

Why row padding stays literal: it contributes directly to `SidebarListStyle.rowExtentOverhead`; tokenizing it would let an app override the token without updating the lazy `ITEM_EXTENT` math. Keep the value as a style geometry constant that matches `space.2`.

## `list.sidebar.*` token values

Keep the existing component tokens, update/add only the needed ones:

| Token | Value |
|---|---|
| `list.sidebar.background` | `{color.surface}` |
| `list.sidebar.foreground` **(update)** | `{color.text.body}` |
| `list.sidebar.selected.background` **(update)** | `{color.selection.subtle}` |
| `list.sidebar.selected.foreground` **(new)** | `{color.text.onSelection}` |
| `list.sidebar.icon.foreground` **(new)** | `{color.icon.muted}` |
| `list.sidebar.selected.icon.foreground` **(new)** | `{color.text.onSelection}` |

No new list-specific dimension tokens are needed: the style references `control.radius`, `control.font.size`, `space.3`, and `space.6` directly.

## Sidebar list + label styling

`SidebarListStyle.makeRow` will:

- Apply a private `SidebarLabelStyle(selected)` to the row content.
- Render the label as `HStack(spacing = space.3)`:
  - icon: `fontSize`/frame `space.6`, foreground `list.sidebar.icon.foreground` or `list.sidebar.selected.icon.foreground`
  - title: `fontSize(control.font.size)`, `FontWeight.SEMIBOLD`, foreground `list.sidebar.foreground` or `list.sidebar.selected.foreground`
- Apply the row background `list.sidebar.selected.background` when selected.
- Apply the row radius `control.radius`.
- Apply a selected/default foreground at row level so non-`Label` row content also follows.
- Use an 8px literal row padding and a 2px top/bottom transparent inset for the Tailwind `space-y-1` gap.
- Leave an explicitly nested `.labelStyle(...)` closer to the `Label` winning, per environment nearest-wins.

The demo then changes its sidebar rows to:

```kotlin
Label(item.label) { Icon(item.icon) }
```

so the list style actually supplies the label presentation.

## No renderer-owned CSS

Everything above is emitted by the composite as normal `BACKGROUND_COLOR`, `COLOR`, `FONT_SIZE`, `SPACING`, `PADDING_*`, and `BORDER_RADIUS` properties with `DESIGN_TOKEN` references. No `.pathland-sidebar` or hover CSS is added.

The one thing a composite cannot express is **hover/pressed styling** without a renderer-owned hook. Since we are avoiding renderer CSS, I would leave hover out and match the static/default/selected design exactly. The selected row remains the keyboard/focus indicator.

## Implementation and verification

- Add the four semantic colors to the design catalog, `spec/TOKENS.md`, and native concrete defaults.
- Update the three existing `list.sidebar.*` tokens and add the three new color tokens to `TIER1_TOKENS`, concrete defaults, design tokens, and `spec/TOKENS.md`.
- Update `SidebarListStyle`/`SidebarLabelStyle` and the demo `NavigationSidebar`.
- Remove the demo theme's `list.sidebar.background` override so the sidebar uses the Tailwind `color.surface` values.
- Update Rust `SidebarListStyle` row padding to 8/8 and apply `control.radius`; Rust has no `Label`, so the label style is JVM-only.
- Regenerate design CSS, sync assets, update the HTML golden fixture, and run:
  - `npm --prefix design run build && npm --prefix design run check`
  - `scripts/sync-design-css.sh`
  - `cargo test -p pathland-view -p pathland-render-core -p pathland-render-html`
  - `mvn -q -pl pathland-view-core -am test`
  - `mvn -q -pl pathland-demo-views-kotlin -am test`
  - `mvn -q -P jvm-only test`

This gives Tailwind’s light/dark sidebar design through semantic tokens and reused scales, with all visuals owned by the composite and no renderer-specific CSS.

    @Test
    fun rendersAWindowedLazyGridWithVirtualExtent() {
        val items = (0 until 100).map { "cell-$it" }
        val root = LazyVGrid(columns = 3, spacing = 8f) {
            ForEach(items) { item, _ -> Text(item).frame(height = 44f) }
        }
        val html = renderer().render(frameOf(root), 1)
        assertTrue(html.contains("data-pathland-lazy-grid=\"1\""), html)
        assertTrue(html.contains("data-pathland-lazy-tracks=\"3\""), html)
        assertTrue(html.contains("data-pathland-item-count=\"34\""), html)
        assertTrue(html.contains("data-pathland-item-extent=\"44px\""), html)
        assertTrue(html.contains("data-pathland-first-item-index=\"0\""), html)
        // Default first window (20) + overscan (2) rows, so trailing = (34-22)*52.
        assertTrue(html.contains("padding-bottom:624px"), html)
    }

    @Test
    fun rendersListStylesWithTokenizedDarkModeChrome() {
        val selection = dev.pathland.view.dsl.LazySelection(signal(0), signal(false))
        val root = dev.pathland.view.dsl.List(
            listOf("one", "two", "three"),
            itemExtent = 44f,
            selection = selection,
        ) { item, _ -> Text(item) }
            .listStyle(dev.pathland.view.dsl.InsetGroupedListStyle)

        val renderer = renderer()
        val html = renderer.render(frameOf(root), 1)
        assertTrue(html.contains("data-pathland-lazy=\"vertical\""), html)
        assertTrue(html.contains("<ul "), "semantic list: $html")
        assertTrue(html.contains("<li "), "semantic rows: $html")
        assertTrue(html.contains("var(--pl-list-group-background"), "group token: $html")
        assertTrue(html.contains("var(--pl-list-separator"), "separator token: $html")

        val css = renderer.baseCss()
        assertTrue(css.contains("--pl-list-background"), "list light token: $css")
        assertTrue(css.contains("--pl-dark-list-background"), "list forced-dark token: $css")
        assertTrue(css.contains("@media (prefers-color-scheme: dark)"), "dark mode media")

Implemented the sidebar label styling with semantic tokens and reused existing scales. Navigation behavior is unchanged (still local sidebar selection).

- Added semantic tokens: `color.text.body`, `color.icon.muted`, `color.selection.subtle`, `color.text.onSelection`.

- Demo sidebar rows now use `Label`, and the demo theme’s sidebar background override was removed so Tailwind’s white/gray-900 surface applies.
- Rust `SidebarListStyle` updated to matching padding, gap, and corner radius.
- No renderer-owned CSS was added; all styling is emitted by the composite. Hover/pressed states remain renderer-owned and were intentionally not added.
- Updated specs, status files, design CSS/assets, HTML golden fixture, and tests.

651:**Complete**: 16-byte opcode engine (`pathland-core`), SwiftUI-style view DSL with decoupled chainable modifiers (`pathland-view`), declarative diff-based reactive emission (`pathland-core`), **reactive signals** (`pathland-core::signal` — writable `Signal` values bound to node text/properties, so a signal change re-emits only the bound nodes, reachable from Java via the `pathland_native_signal_*` / `node_bind_*` C ABI), host reader to a native-element description (`pathland-render-gtk`), opcode transport with network-batch encode/decode + time/size batching policy (`pathland-core-transport`), golden conformance vectors (incl. raw-input EVENT and network-batch bytes), typed raw-input event encode/decode, `no_std` builds, zero-alloc steady-state emission, the **bidirectional event ring** (host → guest EVENT opcodes in shared memory, drained by the host via a generic `pathland_native_drain_events` C ABI — the renderer only writes + wakes), the **GTK4 renderer** (`pathland-render-gtk`) with Rust demos that render through it without touching GTK directly, the **native JVM library set** — `pathland-core` (pure-Java opcode/wire codec, attributed text, and Markdown) and `pathland-view-core` (Kotlin: open `View` interface + shared value/SPI vocabulary, **Angular-parity signals/computed/effects** with synchronous flush, fine-grained retained-tree emitter with **node-level binding effects**, router, cross-platform `StateStore` + **`PersistentState`**) and the opt-in `pathland-native-core` (`dev.pathland.nativecore` — lazy **JNA ring interop** into `libpathland_core`, kept off the server classpath) and the sole JVM authoring DSL `dev.pathland.view.dsl` (SwiftUI-shaped builders, modifier sugar, property-delegate state, navigation/media helpers, styles), `dev.pathland.render.html` (pure-Java port of the Rust HTML renderer; content.text:
Run this from the repo:

```bash
cd lib/java

# Refresh generated design CSS/assets + DOM bundle
mvn -P refresh-ide validate

# Reinstall the changed libraries and demo views into ~/.m2
mvn -DskipTests install
```

Then start Quarkus:

```bash
cd lib/java/pathland-quarkus-demo
mvn quarkus:dev
```

Open `http://localhost:8080/`.

Notes:
- Don’t use `mvn -P refresh-ide install` on its own: that profile excludes demo modules. Use the two-step sequence above, or `mvn -P refresh-ide,demos -DskipTests install`.
- For a faster rebuild, you can target:
  ```bash
  cd lib/java
  mvn -P refresh-ide validate
  mvn -DskipTests -pl pathland-quarkus-demo,pathland-quarkus-deployment -am install
  ```
- Quarkus dev mode uses the installed dependency jars. After changing `pathland-demo-views-kotlin`, `pathland-view-core`, or `pathland-render-html`, reinstall and restart `quarkus:dev`.
- The demo’s default port and ad proxy are both `8080`; keep that port unless you also override `pathland.demo.ad-url`.
